ce:abstract-sec.ce:simple-para: The copolymers consisting of acrylic and methacrylic esters have achieved prime importance due to their versatile environment friendly applications. Copolymerization of Methyl methacrylate (MMA) with suitable vinyl monomers such as alkyl acrylate and methacrylate has been carried out for modifying the properties of the polymer. In current research synthesis of waterborne copolymer of MMA and 2- Ethyl hexyl acrylate (2-EHA) carried out by ecofriendly emulsion polymerization technique and the kinetics of polymerization, characterizations of the copolymers have been studied. Synthesized copolymers were characterized by FTIR, NMR, DSC, and TGA. The kinetics results of the MMA-co-EHA copolymer was compared with the previously synthesized copolymer MMA with Butyl acrylate (BA). On comparing these results, it was found that EHA gives higher conversion with respect to BA under the same reaction conditions. Out of all the prepared latexes some are suitable for binder purposes in environment friendly water borne coating applications.

ce:section.ce:para: Copolymer synthesis is important in several areas due to the wide range of properties that can be achieved from the combination of different monomers. The copolymers consisting of acrylic and methacrylic esters have achieved prime importance due to their versatile applications [1–3] in medicine, pharmaceuticals, paints, polymer activities and rubbers. Copolymerization of methyl methacrylate (MMA) with suitable vinyl monomers such as alkyl acrylate and methacrylate has been carried out for modifying the properties of the polymer. The length of the alkyl group in these alkyl acrylates has pronounced effects on the flexibility of methacrylate polymers. The increase in the side chain length of the esters derived from straight chain alcohol usually softens the polymer.

Acrylic polymers cover a wide range of physical properties. Depending on the monomers selected and the method of polymerization the acrylate esters produce internal plasticization of the polymers resulting in improved toughness, increased tensile strength, increased tear and impact strengths and improved process ability. The selection of the monomer and monomer ratios in the copolymerization play a vital role in designing the copolymers for the use in the coatings and paint applications. 2-Ethyl hexylacrylate (EHA) is a very useful monomer in number of industrial applications. The poly (ethyl hexyl acylate) (PEHA) has very low glass transition temperature (Tg = −65 °C) and also it has excellent film formation property [4]. The copolymers of PEHA with other acrylates, methacrylates, esters, vinyl acetate, vinyl chloride, etc. find applications in adhesives, coatings, leather, plasticizers, chemical intermediates, textiles and in many plastics [5,6].

n-Butyl acrylate (BA), 2-ethyl hexyl acrylate (EHA), and MMA monomers specifically are used in adhesive production and coating applications as binders in household paints [7,8] largely because their different glass transition temperatures allow for the control the application properties [9,10]. The Tg of PMMA and PBA are 100 °C and −49 °C respectively.

The kinetics of copolymerization of MMA with BA and their characterization has been discussed in previous study [11]. The aim of this research to prepare a environment friendly latex and to study the kinetics of copolymerization of MMA and 2-EHA. The characterizations of the copolymers will be studied to see the effect of higher acrylate (2-EHA) on the kinetics of polymerization. The structural characterization of the copolymer was performed by FTIR and 1H NMR. The reactivity ratios in the copolymerization determined for the classical copolymerization model using the methods of Fineman-Ross (F-R) and Kelen-Tudos (K-T). Copolymerization is the most successful and powerful method for effecting systematic changes in polymer properties. Monomer reactivity ratios are very important quantitative values to predict the copolymer composition.

Monomers MMA and EHA (Merck Ltd., New Delhi, India) were purified before use by alkali wash method. Free radical initiator potassium persulfate (KPS), emulsifier sodium lauryl sulphate (SLS; Thomas baker Mumbai, Maharashtra, India) and aluminium sulfate (Thomas baker Mumbai, Maharashtra, India) were used as received. Deionized water was used throughout the experimental work.

The polymerization reactions were carried out in a 500-mL three-necked round-bottomed (RB) flask equipped with reflux condenser, stirrer, dropping funnel, and thermometer. Pre-emulsions of monomers were prepared by taking MMA and EHA in the molar ratio 9:1, 8:2, 7:3, 6:4, and 5:5 (sample designations SE1, SE2, SE3, SE4, and SE5, respectively Table 1 ). The synthesis of latex was done by the emulsion polymerization of monomers (MMA and EHA). Pre-emulsion solution was prepared by adding two third of the total emulsifier required SLS in the recipe, water (250 ml) and the mixture of monomers as per the molar ratio given in the Table into a beaker. The content were agitated for 30 min and kept for 10 min to check the stability of the emulsion. If separation of the two phases was observed the contents were agitated for another 10 min. This exercise was repeated until stable emulsion was obtained. Once the pre-emulsion was found to be stable this mixture was used for polymerization. The remaining one third of emulsifier was dissolved in water (200 ml) and taken in the three-necked RB flask and the contents were heated at 70 ± 1 °C under nitrogen atmosphere. The initiator solution was prepared separately by dissolving potassium per sulfate (KPS) in water (150 ml). The pre-emulsion and initiator solution were added to the flask slowly during a period of about 30 min under constant stirring. The polymerizations were carried out for 3 h. The obtained latex was coagulated by using aqueous aluminium sulfate solution and filtered to get polymer. The polymer was dried at 60 ± 1 °C in hot air oven.
FTIR spectra of various polymers were recorded in the range 400–4000 cm−1 using a Perkin Elmer RXI spectrophotometer use pellets of potassium bromide.

The composition of the synthesized copolymers (SE1 to SE5) was determined by comparing the intensities of the OCH3 and OCH2 proton resonances on the 1H Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra at 302 K in a deuteriochloroform (CDCl3) solution using Bruker WM 250 spectrometer operating at 400 MHz. The composition of the synthesized copolymer was determined by comparing the intensities of the chemical shifts. The composition of the copolymer was calculated by the formula was discussed in detail for the copolymerization of MMA-BA copolymer in characterization part of previous publication [12].

Copolymerization often brings about drastic changes in the mechanical and physical properties of the polymer. The most important physical property to be affected is the glass transition temperature (Tg). DSC is a suitable technique for quantitative measurements of parameters such as heat capacity, heat of fusion, heat of crystallization and Tg of polymers etc. The Tg of polymers was determined using TA instruments, TA Q20 at a heating rate of 10 °C/min under nitrogen atmosphere. The Tg was determined from the step transition in the thermograms of copolymers taken by DSC. For the prediction of Tg of copolymers on basis of the composition of monomer component. It has been observed that the net effect of the interaction between two monomeric components of a copolymer on the Tg value is as through the copolymer is a mixture of two homopolymers. The Tg value of random copolymers therefore depends on the Tg value of the individual homopolymers and on the ratio of the two monomeric components. In order to characterize this transition, which can be attributed to glass transition, three characteristic temperatures were noted.
Ton = Temperature at which deviation from the base line starts. It was obtained by extrapolating the base line and drawing tangent at the steep portion of the curve.
Tg = Temperature at the inflection point of the transition.
Tf = Temperature at which base line again becomes straight. It was obtained by extrapolation.
The thermal stability of polymers was determined by using TA instruments, TA Q50 at a heating rate of 20 °C/min under nitrogen atmosphere.

The percentage conversions of polymer obtained were plotted against time for particular reaction condition. The value of the rate constant (k) for the polymerization reaction at varying reaction parameters were obtained from the slope of plot between ln ([Mt]/[Mo]) and time, where Mt is conversion at time t (min) and M0 is the total monomer concentration.

The effect of the monomer feed ratio on the kinetics of emulsion polymerization of MMA/EHA was studied by keeping the constant concentration of SLS and KPS, 2.8 × 10−2 mol/L and 7.9 × 10−3 mol/L, respectively gave higher conversion in case of copolymers of MMA and BA [11]. The molar feed ratio of MMA: EHA were varied as 9:1, 8:2, 7:3, 6:4 and 5:5, the reaction was carried out at 70 ± 1 °C under Nitrogen atmosphere. The percentage was determined gravimetrically by withdrawing samples at different time intervals. The conversion at varying molar ratio has been plotted as a function of time and the plots are shown in Fig. 1 a. It is apparent from the Figure that as the concentration of EHA increased in monomer feed the conversion increased.

The increase in conversion was observed up to 3 h of reaction time and it is apparent from the plots that it level off after ∼2 h reaction time. The conversion at 2 h for SE1, SE2, SE3, SE4, and SE5 were 65.4%, 78.4%, 80.1%, 87.3%, and 90.7%, respectively. It is also clear from the data that as the EHA content in the feed increases, the conversion at any time increased. These results when compared to the conversion in case of MMA/BA copolymerization [11], it was found that at the same molar ratio of the feed and at the same reaction time, the conversion was higher when EHA was used as a comonomer in comparison to BA.

On comparing these results, it was found that EHA gives higher conversion with respect to BA. This may be due to the fact that the EHA has higher propagation rate coefficient [20] in comparison to MMA and BA. The more hydrophobic the carboxylic comonomer the faster is the rate of polymerization. In our case the EHA monomer is more hydrophobic in nature than the MMA and BA, and therefore it was found that the rate of polymerization increases in presence of it. The MMA radicals are tertiary radicals and hence are much less reactive for hydrogen abstraction than the secondary EHA radicals so EHA increases the conversion of monomers.

The structural characterization of synthesized copolymers designated as SE1, SE2, SE3, SE4, and SE5 were analyzed by FTIR spectroscopy. The FTIR of all the synthesized copolymers were found to be similar. All the copolymers exhibits the characteristics bands associated with acrylates. The IR spectra of a typical sample of copolymer have been presented in Fig. 2 . The absence of absorption band at 1600 cm−1 in the spectra indicated that no acrylate monomer was present as impurity in the copolymer.

All the copolymers shows 2995 cm−1, C–H Stretching (asymmetric); 2953 cm−1, CH Stretching (symmetric);1730 cm−1, CO Stretching; 1271 cm−1, 1240 cm−1, COC (asymmetric); 1190, 1148 cm−1, COC esters and 989 cm−1, 842 cm−1; ester skeletal vibrations. Other prominent absorption peaks were at 1454 cm−1 and 1400 cm−1, these are due to asymmetrical and symmetrical bending vibrations of CCH3, respectively. The small peak near 3445 cm−1 showed the presence of OH stretching which may be due to the presence of residual water in the copolymer.

Kelen-Tudos (K-T) and Fineman-Ross (F-R) methods were used for calculating r1 and r2 values. The reactivity ratios were determined using the copolymer composition data obtained by the ratio of the peak areas of OCH2 and OCH3 protons in the respective NMR spectra. The corresponding F-R and K-T plots for the MMA-co-EHA copolymers are shown in Figs. 4 and 5
and the values of r1 and r2 are given in Table 5 .

The above values of r1 and r2 were determined using the least square method (R2 ≥ 0.98). Reactivity results in a slight deviation from ideality. Since r1 < r2 < 1, resulting copolymers tend to be random in nature and are slightly richer in EHA during the polymerization. The tendency of monomers to copolymerize is noted by r value between zero and unity. r1 is greater than unity means that M1* preferentially adds M1 instead of M2, while r1 < 1 means that M* preferentially adds M2. An r1 value of zero would mean that M1 is incapable of undergoing homopolymerization. In our case r1 < 1 shows that MMA preferentially adds to EHA monomer unit by the following mechanism.

The glass transition temperatures of the copolymers of MMA-EHA were determined by DSC analysis at 10 °C/min under nitrogen atmosphere. The DSC scans from the from −50 °C to 100 °C of all the copolymers designated as SE1, SE2, SE3, SE4, and SE5 are given in Fig. 6 . The characteristics temperatures Ton, Tg and Tf of PMMA and the synthesized copolymers are given in the following Table 6 .

The Tg of the copolymers lie between the Tg’s of the corresponding homoploymers. The Tg observed by thermogram obtained by DSC and Tg determined by Fox have been plotted in Fig. 7 . It is apparent from the Figure that the theoretical value of Tg were higher than the experimental Tg. The theoretical Tg for SE3 polymer was 12.2 °C while experimentally it was found to be 8.1 °C. This may be due to the difference in the copolymer composition and sequence distribution in the polymer chain. In case of copolymers Ton, Tg and Tf decreases with the increase in EHA content in the feed. Polymer chain flexibility and interaction energy between molecules and attraction forces of atoms have an important role on Tg. If a comonomer with low Tg is added, the Tg of the main structure will decrease. SE2, SE3, and SE4 are suitable for coating application as the Tg of these copolymers lie in the range 0–40 °C as reported by Schall et al. [24]

The thermal stability of copolymers was investigated by thermogravimetric analysis. The TG and DTG scans of the copolymers are shown in Fig. 8 . The relative thermal stability of the copolymer samples were assessed by comparing by the following characteristics temperature:

Initial Decomposition Temperature (Ti): It is defined as the temperature at which the decomposition of the sample begins as indicated by a deviation linearity in the thermogram. It was determined by extrapolation using the sleep, portion of weight loss curve and the initial base line.
Final Decomposition Temp (Tf): It is the temperature at which decomposition was almost completed. It was also obtained by extrapolation of the steepest portion and end regions of weight loss curve.

Temperature of Maximum rate of weight loss (Tmax): It is defined as the temp at which the rate of weight loss is maximum. It was obtained from DTG curve and the temperature corresponding to the peak position was Tmax. The results of thermal behavior are summarized and given in Table 7 .

All the copolymers showed characteristic single step weight loss [25] due to the decomposition of ester linkages. It is clear from the table that the initial temperature of decomposition increased from 149 °C to 220 °C when EHA content in the feed increased from 10 to 50 wt%. However, there is no significant variation in Tf and Tmax for all the copolymers. It is also evident from the nature of the thermograms that once the decomposition starts, the pattern for the decomposition of all the copolymers were similar indicating that the mechanism of decomposition is similar. The increase in Ti with the increase of comonomer EHA in the feed.

The results presented in this article demonstrate that at the same molar ratio of the feed and at the same reaction time, the monomer conversion was higher when higher acrylate EHA was used as a comonomer with MMA in comparison to BA. This may be due to the fact that the EHA has higher propagation rate coefficient in comparison to MMA and BA. The more hydrophobic the carboxylic comonomer the faster is the rate of polymerization. In our case the EHA monomer is more hydrophobic in nature than the MMA and BA, and therefore it was found that the rate of polymerization increases in presence of it. The MMA radicals are tertiary radicals and hence are much less reactive for hydrogen abstraction than the secondary EHA radicals so EHA increases the conversion of monomers. It was found that the tendency of monomers to copolymerize is noted by r value between zero and unity. The prepared latexes SE2, SE3, and SE4 are suitable for coating application as the Tg of these copolymers lie in the range 0–40 °C. Due to use of water as a vehicle this technique is water borne and environment friendly, because as we know most of the binders used in coatings are solvent borne. In all the copolymers characteristic single step weight loss found due to the decomposition of ester linkages shows the thermal stability of binders.
